claims.claim: Story cutscenes suffer from heavy lag, stuttering, and audio desynchronization.

citations.review_text:
From the second I launched it, the intro stuttered — video freezing, audio breaking up, the whole thing a laggy mess. Gameplay itself seemed fine, but I didn't get far, because sitting through story cutscenes in that state was infuriating.

This isn't my hardware. The video playback clearly wasn't built for modern CPUs. Happy to revise this review once it's fixed.

Cutscene performance is shocking, regardless of resolution or graphics quality. Driving mechanics and handling are annoying, especially if you are playing with controller. Audio is constantly desynced. Glad I only paid £3 for this and not full price. Your money is best spent elsewhere.

HORRIBLE optimization, cinematic scenes stutter like CRAZY, even on low quality, and then crashes the game... 
Tried a bunch of fixes suggested online, but to no avail.

Dang :(

Every single story cutscene suffers from massive lag, stuttering, and severe FPS drops. The audio constantly desyncs from the video, turning every cinematic into a total mess. THERE IS NO NORMAL SOLUTION TO THIS PROBLEM. I have searched the entire internet, and every community guide or "fix" is either useless or doesn't work. The game forces a 30 FPS cap during cinematics that completely breaks the performance even on high-end PCs. The developers totally abandoned the game with this bug.Do not buy this if you care about the story mode. It is a literal slideshow.

Optimization doesn't exist for PC at all in this game, you'll often see stutters during cutscenes and normal gameplay. Very disappointing. If you want to play the game in a more "stable" environment, play it on PS5 or Xbox Series.
The cutscenes lagged so much so I had to return the game. I got it for a 95% discount during Spring Sale and returned during that period only.

Doesn't run well, cutscenes are extremely laggy and have synch issues.

An astonishingly poor excuse for a racing title that fails on the most fundamental levels... I cannot recommend this to anyone...

1. The Mandatory EA App
Purchasing a game on Steam only to be held hostage by a bloated, unnecessary third-party launcher is an exhausting anti-consumer practice. It adds zero value and nothing but friction between the player and the main menu.

2. Zero Steering Wheel Support

claims.claim: Players must install the EA app launcher and create an account to play the game.

citations.review_text:
It's not bad but ultimately the negatives outweigh the positives. 

The bad: 
- It's an EA game so you will have to install their launcher, create and account, and then you will have to deal with the EA app launching by default on startup, etc.
- The cops are rubberbandy as hell. When the heat level goes up, no matter how fast you're going some cop will spawn behind you at a thousand miles an hour and ram you to the middle of next week. You're supposed to use ramps and gimmicks like that, good old fashioned driving won't help you. This was a dealbreaker for me.
- I didn't like the soundtrack, way too much reggeatón.

The good: Some solid NFS action, great graphics, cool cars, very good sound. The handling is very arcade, more than I expected, but it was still fun for a little bit.

Controller setup is atrocious. I own a good Hall Effect controller (I can't configure it, thanks EA) and I'm not about to buy another one just for this game. I absolutely hate that EA forces its bloated launcher on you even when playing through Steam. Extremely frustrating and unnecessary. Come on, EA — just let us play the damn game.

I'll never buy another EA game.

citations.review_text: The game overall is quite good. The graphics and quality are amazing as well. The story is quite different from what a person would expect from a racing game, which makes this even better. Though, the cutscenes may lag in between but that does not have anything to do with your PC or laptop if the gameplay is smooth.

The game’s a blast, classic Need for Speed vibes. It’s not the best in the series, but it’s solid all around. The graphics are slick, and the cars look super detailed. Gameplay feels good, and the events are balanced. The story’s pretty light, but at least it’s not overly wordy.

There are two significant downsides, though: the cutscenes were stuttering like hell on my modern PC, no matter what I tried, borderless mode, no overlays, FPS caps, you name it. And the cops are way too powerful at night (I played on Medium difficulty), until you get a car over 350. It’s really frustrating when you get busted almost every time, and it just feels like a waste of time.

If you can get over these 2 things, I recommend to any NFS fan or simply to arcade racing lovers.

claims.claim: The main story is described as short and featuring poorly written dialogue and characters.

citations.review_text: Best Graphics ive evre seen by far the best nfs game to ever come out  cutimization is on another level the speed of the cars dont feel over exadrated the story is a little short thats my only complaint

Honestly disappointing.

Pros:
- Driving. Handling of cars feel satisfying. You can tune them to your liking and drive them the way you like.
- Online play. Had fun encounters and races with other players.
- Map. It has different surfaces, elevations, locations. You can either drive in the city, in the mountains or in the swamp. Chose whichever you like.

Cons:
- Main story. It's short, poorly written ( feels AI generated ). Honestly such an unsatisfying feeling when you finish the main story. I literally said out loud : " is this it? "
-Characters. All of them are boring, have cringe voice lines copied from tiktoks and say things that make no sense in the situation. I could be drifting in to a wall, knocking out every light pole and destroying my vehicle, but some side character is going to praise my " W driving " ... Their voice lines make them all feel like teenagers watching online live stream.
- Police. This is the most frustrating part about normal gameplay. Police will randomly start chasing you even if you are just parked motionless, breaking no laws. It makes no sense. They attack you not because you where breaking the law but because you exist within their radius. It's like the most lazy coded police i've seen in games of modern time. They will just randomly accelerate 0-350 km/h in 1 sec out of nowhere because that's how physics work for them in this game. And as they chase you more will spawn in front out of nowhere. You can literally see them spawn in and drop down from thin air. Early game running from them feels stupid until you discover that you can go to race track, drive in circles and they magically lose sight of you even if you keep passing them by going in circles. Damage they deal to you also is unproportionally unfair to what you deal back to them. Just stupid and takes you out of the immersion of the fun parts  of this game
- EA. Can't be played unless EA app is installed into your device.
- Cars. Surprisingly there where not that…

The Ending was so sudden that it left me a bit shocked and unsatisfied. But despite that, story doesn't really matter much to me in this game, altho it could've been done a lot better and more intense. Some dialogue also a bit cringy to me. Facial expression is a bit scary at time. 

All of that doesn't deter the fact that this game is so much fun to play, and that's what really matter to this game. The driving and racing mechanic is smooth for an arcade game. At first i didn't like it, since i was transitioned from a semi-realistic forza horizon 4 to fully arcade-y heat. But the more i understand and learned it, it became a blast. It's so fun to pulled of smooth turning. There are so much races to do in the game and each feels unique. It also supported with the world being so fun to explore, even tho i haven't explored the off-road area much. The graphic looks fantastic, so eyecatching and satisfying. The car detail look sleek and shiny. The physic is hilarious tho, because we can almost crash into every object, even some big trees, so the game is less punishing. The drift is a lot easier than what i've experienced in forza horizon. My favorite event is sprint race, compared to a circuit one. There are also difficulty you can choose.

The only thing that i probably didn't like much is the soundtrack selection could've been better. And also i've spoiled with all the collectibles because i have the key maps dlc, that i forgot its not part of the game, and i just forgot to turn it off or uninstall it everytime. The world feels like lack of variety. and the city part looks too similar to the other. 

I still have to try all the cars and get to the maximum reputation (level). As for now, this game is a 9/10. Feels like a sweet spot to put it even higher.

Title: Need for Speed Heat – An Adrenaline-Fueled Street Racing Experience

Review:
Need for Speed Heat is an exciting open-world racing game that combines high-speed street racing with intense police chases. The vibrant city of Palm City looks stunning, especially with its day-and-night cycle that changes the gameplay experience. Customizing cars is deep and rewarding, while the fast-paced races and thrilling pursuits keep the action nonstop. Whether you're building your dream ride or outrunning the cops, Need for Speed Heat delivers an adrenaline rush that racing fans will love.

Rating: ★★★★☆

claims.claim: Reviewers state that drifting and offroad racing campaigns are very short and lack depth.

citations.review_text:
Great arcade-style racing game. It has its flaws but is overall a good instalment in the NFS franchise.

Pros
- The graphics. My entry level gaming laptop runs this game flawlessly.
- The map is also giant and never feels like I'm running out of road.
- The car selection is also wide and has many classics from other racing games and pop culture.
- The story is pretty basic but is decent enough for the type of game this is.
- Car upgrades are simple but done well, I also feel like I'm not having to grind too much to afford the high tier upgrades

Cons
- You can tell this game was rushed out, balancing is nowhere to be seen and certain aspects of the game are lacking content
- Drifting and offroad races and their stories are forgotten about; the drifting campaign can be completed in about 15 minutes and the races all feel the same with very low stakes. Offroad is done slightly better but still not great; the racing feels amazing, but its' story is just as short as the drifting one.
- The "performance rating" the game gives your car is strictly based on its' road performance, meaning if you want to build a car for offroad or drifting, it will have a very low PR score despite it being the best in class.
- The drifting mechanics are frustrating, rather than a realistic drifting experience like what you would find in games like Forza, there is a sort of "drifting mode" your car goes into when you double tap the gas button which can be annoying when not trying to drift. Once you do enter into the "drift mode" the car wants to either spin out or stop drifting altogether. The AI drivers have trouble with this mechanic as well, explains the single player drift races.

While I have expressed my distain for the drifting quite a bit, it's not a large part of the game, I beat the main story before even touching the drift section. My biggest gripe, and the only one that actually effects the average player, is the "night mode." The game is separated into two modes: d…

The Ending was so sudden that it left me a bit shocked and unsatisfied. But despite that, story doesn't really matter much to me in this game, altho it could've been done a lot better and more intense. Some dialogue also a bit cringy to me. Facial expression is a bit scary at time. 

All of that doesn't deter the fact that this game is so much fun to play, and that's what really matter to this game. The driving and racing mechanic is smooth for an arcade game. At first i didn't like it, since i was transitioned from a semi-realistic forza horizon 4 to fully arcade-y heat. But the more i understand and learned it, it became a blast. It's so fun to pulled of smooth turning. There are so much races to do in the game and each feels unique. It also supported with the world being so fun to explore, even tho i haven't explored the off-road area much. The graphic looks fantastic, so eyecatching and satisfying. The car detail look sleek and shiny. The physic is hilarious tho, because we can almost crash into every object, even some big trees, so the game is less punishing. The drift is a lot easier than what i've experienced in forza horizon. My favorite event is sprint race, compared to a circuit one. There are also difficulty you can choose.

The only thing that i probably didn't like much is the soundtrack selection could've been better. And also i've spoiled with all the collectibles because i have the key maps dlc, that i forgot its not part of the game, and i just forgot to turn it off or uninstall it everytime. The world feels like lack of variety. and the city part looks too similar to the other. 

I still have to try all the cars and get to the maximum reputation (level). As for now, this game is a 9/10. Feels like a sweet spot to put it even higher.

Very replayable racing game. NFS Heat has a very short story, but a very interesting one. I can feel what Ghost was trying to achieve, trying to make a connection/driver-to-vehicle-bond, but they didn't make it exactly right. There is actually a purpose to the story which already ranks it higher than Unbound imo. Physics are very finniky at high speeds, but that's part of the fun. Cops are dangerous and shouldn't be underestimated, hightening the thrill, especially when you bank your first 1,000,000 REP in one night. The day/sytem is awesome, a great concept that needs just a little work, but still great as it is now.
There are so many mods in this game it is crazy. You could probably complete the game, replace every single car in the game and replay it, or overhaul the game with graphics and features, or add new customisations, make cars go insane speeds, make the cops even more unescapable, sit at the upgrade menu listening to the turbo flutter for 3 hours straight, turn a Mclaren into a Rally car, give it simcade physics to completely mess up all muscle memory... Seriously, you can make it feel like a whole new game. Highly recommended. And no, people buy UNBOUND because it's new gen and way better looking.  The story is garbage, the freeroam system feels limited and those cartoon character make me wanna be with Allah. NFS is dead, play any other game bar UNBOUND.

citations.review_text:
The game is good but the story is short which means there is no motivation to unlock cars unless car pleases your eyes. Once you get the RSR (at level 16) and RX-7, you're good to go for the entire game.
Coming to the customization, some cars have such kits that will please your eyes whereas others will either trick your eyes or straight up bleed it.
The game really shines when it come to collectibles. I absolutely love collecting them. In fact, I like it more than the story itself.

Alright, played over 520 hours, finished the main story 13 times and planning to play more,

I'm giving this review solely from a singpleplayer perspective because that's my arcade racing kick, 

let's dive into the pros and cons, some of the points will intertwine for both,

PROS -

1. Story: It's short but decent enough to keep you engaged. I like the characters, both the villains and the allies. They set the tone serious just enough to feel immersive but not too much so that it spirals away from the street racing vibes. The tone is balanced.

2. Cars/Customization: A decent collection for NFS, LOVE the visual customization and the uniqueness of the cars. The performance upgrades feel good too.

3. Races: Maybe not for all, but I love the offroading. So normal sprints/circuits, drifts and offroads, all are there and the tracks are fun to race on.

4. Day Night: The most creative aspect of this game I think. You can switch to night anytime. Day races are legal, on sanctioned tracks and you earn cash. Night races are the main street races with cops and traffic, they give you reputation or rep.
Rep levels unlocks cars and upgrades, and cash is to afford them. A very well balanced currency dynamic.

5. Cops: Highly challenging, brutal, very aggressive and WILL ram you to oblivion. But can be evaded using tactics and specific places (ramp jumps etc.)
And of course, the heat level. The rep points from night races and evading cops will multiply based on which heat level you ended the night on. It's a great risk-reward mechanic.
If you get busted, the multiplied points will go away, you'll only end with the base rep.
I love the thrill even though I'm unskilled.

6. Map: I think it's the BEST map in the entire series. Large, diverse, gorgeous and captured that beachside city aesthetics fairly well.
The beauty truly shines in the night with neon lights and signs. It's a joy to race both in day and night time.
And even outside racing, it feels good just to drive around, gett…

Need for Speed Heat is one of the best modern games in the NFS series. The day-night cycle works surprisingly well: daytime races are focused on making money, while nighttime races are about building reputation and engaging in risky chases with the police. Palm City looks stunning, especially at night with all the neon lights and rain reflections.

The career mode is top-notch, with a well-designed economy that requires you to think about what to buy and how to spend your money. The car customization is excellent and offers plenty of freedom to create your own style. Police chases can be intense and sometimes chaotic, which adds a lot of excitement. The main downside is that the story is quite short, and the ending can feel repetitive. However, if you like arcade racing, customization, and fast-paced police chases, this game is definitely worth playing.
